findings.title: deleteCache handler throws plain Error instead of TRPCError
findings.body: When the credential isn't found or doesn't belong to the caller, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps unknown errors to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (HTTP 500) and, depending on error formatting, can surface the raw message. This conflates an authorization/not-found condition with a server failure, breaks client error handling (which only shows a generic toast), and pollutes error monitoring with false 500s. Use `TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" | "FORBIDDEN" })` as the other handlers in this router do.

findings.title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates the connectedCalendars query
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop, unlike `disconnectMutation` which invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in `onSettled`. In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` the `onSuccess`/`onChanged` prop is optional and is not passed on the installed-calendars page, so after a successful cache deletion the dropdown keeps displaying the old "Last updated" timestamp and still offers "Delete cached data" until a manual reload (the query is also configured with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`). Add `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` to the mutation's settled/success handler.

findings.title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, so expired cache is reported as fresh
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `calendarCache` rows for the credential and returns `max(updatedAt)` without filtering on `expiresAt >= now()`. Cache rows that are already expired (and therefore never served by `getCachedAvailability`) still produce a `cacheUpdatedAt` value, so the UI reports a cache as present/"last updated" when there is effectively no usable cache. Filter on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to match the read path.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars widened to require updatedAt/googleChannelId without need
findings.body: `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` in their `Pick<SelectedCalendar, ...>` types, but neither field is read anywhere in this module. This is an exported public type consumed by other callers (platform libraries, API handlers, tests) that build the user object with only `externalId`/`integration`/`eventTypeId` selected; they will now fail type-checking and must all add the two selections (only `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` was updated here). Either revert the widening or update all construction sites.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data to bump updatedAt
findings.body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is issued after every cache refresh with an empty `data` object, relying on Prisma implicitly setting the `@updatedAt` field. This is undocumented behavior (an empty `updateMany` can be a no-op), so the intended timestamp bump may silently never happen, while every cache refresh still pays for an extra write/row lock across all SelectedCalendar rows of the credential. The PR description itself notes this value isn't consumed by the frontend (the UI uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`); either set the field explicitly (`{ updatedAt: new Date() }`) or drop the call.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId accepts the wrong Prisma input type
findings.body: The `data` parameter is typed `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`, but `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany` expects `SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`. `UpdateInput` permits nested relation writes (e.g. `credential: { connect: ... }`) which `updateMany` cannot execute, so such a call type-checks but fails at runtime. Use `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`.

findings.title: Cache timestamp hardcoded to en-US locale and browser timezone
findings.body: The timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, so non-English users see an American date/time format inside an otherwise localized string, and the user's configured timezone/time format preference (12h/24h) is ignored. Use the user's locale (available from `useLocale()`) and the existing date-formatting helpers.

findings.title: Cache status query bypasses the calendar-cache feature gate
findings.body: The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly instead of going through the `CalendarCache.init()` factory that returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the calendar-cache feature is disabled. As a result, cache status (and therefore the "Cache Status"/"Delete cached data" UI) is reported from leftover DB rows even for users/teams where calendar cache is turned off, and an extra DB groupBy runs on every connectedCalendars request regardless of the flag.

findings.title: No tests for the new destructive deleteCache mutation or cache-status repository method
findings.body: `deleteCacheHandler` performs a destructive `calendarCache.deleteMany` gated only by an ownership lookup, and `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` is new query logic, yet neither has unit tests. In particular there is no test asserting that a user cannot delete the cache of another user's credential (the main security property of this endpoint) nor that the credential-id-to-timestamp mapping is correct.

findings.title: Dev script uses macOS-only `sed -i ''` and a CWD-relative .env path
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax; with GNU sed (Linux/CI) the empty string is parsed as the input filename and the command fails with "can't read : No such file or directory", leaving GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL unchanged. Additionally `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the current working directory, so running the script from the repository root creates/edits a `.env` in the repo's parent directory instead of the intended file. Use a path derived from the script location and a portable in-place edit.

findings.title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` without declaring tsx as a dependency
findings.body: `dev:cron` now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` but `tsx` is not listed in this package's dependencies/devDependencies, so `npx` will attempt to download it from the network on every run (failing in offline/locked-down environments and ignoring the yarn lockfile), while the now-unused `ts-node` devDependency remains. Add `tsx` as a devDependency and invoke it via the local binary.

findings.title: Migration header warning contradicts the statement it documents
findings.body: The generated warning block states the column is "Added the required column `updatedAt` ... without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the actual ALTER TABLE adds the column with `DEFAULT NOW()`. Leaving the stale warning in place misleads reviewers/operators into thinking the migration will fail on a non-empty CalendarCache table. Remove or correct the comment.
